Homophily_violation shows the strongest tail signal (p99=0.6924, p99/p50≈6.6×), indicating prevalent feature-neighborhood mismatches despite moderate homophily (0.5334). Community shows the second-strongest tail (p99=0.6516, p99/p50≈6.5×), and with 10 communities and modularity 0.2432, there is meaningful community structure to violate. Clique_density, though scoring low in absolute terms (mean=0.0443), is explicitly recommended as a structural companion to subgraph_contrast to cover injected cliques and collusion rings—complementary to the contextual and attribute-based signals. Together these four paradigms span local subgraph structure, feature-structure alignment, community membership, and structural closure, covering contextual, attribute, structural, and population-level anomaly populations on a degree-heterogeneous sparse graph."
}
